text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000181 bills 99215 at roughly three times the risk-adjusted expectation; the panel skews complex, but the excess persists within every complexity tier, and documentation is too thin to resolve it.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely sicker than average, with most visits on patients with several chronic conditions. Only a small share of this provider's 99215s fall on low-complexity patients, which argues against crude upcoding on simple visits. However, the 99215 share runs about double the all-provider share in every complexity tier, including 0- and 1-condition patients. The sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0104645, C0105873 and C0104616 carry only back pain, obesity or a single stable condition, which is hard to reconcile with high MDM. The few charts returned all supported the billed level and showed no cloning signal, but five records (well under 1% of claims) are far too few to lean either way. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and a random set of 99215s in the 2-4 condition tiers, checking documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
